title: Skill Template
description: A canonical template for a class of skills, derived from accumulated skill_section_preference data. Each template_id encodes the preferred structure, word counts, formatting patterns, and anti-patterns for a skill kind. Templates are the output of section-preference accumulation — they are not hand-authored from scratch; they crystallize from operator verdict data over time. A skill that conforms to a high-quality template gets higher prior probability of promotion.

template_version.description: Semver version string. Increments when section requirements or recommended formats change materially.

applies_to_skill_kind.description: The skill kind this template governs. workflow = step-by-step execution skill. recipe = a pattern or protocol to follow. preflight = checklist run before an action. gate = decision/guard that blocks or permits. domain_expert = contextual knowledge skill (no execution steps). other = cross-kind or experimental.

template_description.description: Plain-language description of when this template applies. What distinguishes this template from others of the same skill_kind.

sections.description: Ordered list of sections the template requires or recommends. Order matches the canonical section ordering in a well-shaped SKILL.md.

required.description: True = a skill that omits this section fails template validation. False = recommended but optional.

recommended_word_count_range.description: Inclusive [min, max] word count for this section. Derived from brevity_score across accumulated section_preference rows. Null = no constraint data yet.

recommended_format_examples.description: Short illustrative examples of well-formed content for this section. Drawn from promoted skills that match this template. Each is a 1-3 line excerpt.

anti_patterns.description: Section-specific anti-patterns that have been rejected in skill_section_preference rows. Each is a short phrase naming the failure mode.

example_skill_ids.description: Slugs of promoted skills that are exemplary instances of this template. Used as positive references when drafting new skills.

last_updated_at.description: When this template was last revised. Increments when derived_from_section_preference_count crosses a threshold that triggers re-derivation.

derived_from_section_preference_count.description: Number of skill_section_preference rows that informed this template version. Low counts = template is mostly hand-authored. High counts = template is data-derived and stable.

examples.template_description: Workflow skills that enforce a gad-ecosystem behavioral discipline — a rule that agents must follow at a specific lifecycle trigger. Characterized by: a standing trigger (not a one-off task), a verifiable success state via gad CLI, and a failure mode that has been observed in the wild. Based on 9 proto-skills drafted 2026-05-09 from the token-drain incident.

recommended_format_examples: Workers must call completeHandoff themselves — never delegate to the child runtime
Reach for gad ask / gad subcommands before Glob+Read+Grep cascades on planning data
anti_patterns: Vague noun phrase without an agent subject ('handoff completion behavior')
Missing the key constraint word ('never', 'always', 'before', 'after')

recommended_format_examples: Any time you are writing, reviewing, or debugging a worker loop that dispatches work to a child runtime.
Any time you need to answer a question about the GAD ecosystem. The CLI is the cheap path.
anti_patterns: Restating the description without adding scope context
Using 'when X happens' without saying who the agent is or what system context applies

recommended_format_examples:
- "handoffs show completed_at null"
- "implementing a worker loop"
- "claim leak review"

- "reading TASK-REGISTRY.xml"
- "what tasks are in phase N"
- "grep on DECISION-REGISTRY.xml"
anti_patterns: Generic category phrases ('working with handoffs', 'managing tasks') that match dozens of unrelated operations
Triggers that require prior skill knowledge to parse ('evolution sweep overdue' without defining what overdue means)
Fewer than 4 trigger phrases — insufficient for reliable cold-agent matching

recommended_format_examples: - Every handoff shows non-null completed_at — verifiable via `gad handoffs show <id>`
- `gad tasks list --phase N | grep '"skill": null'` returns 0 results
anti_patterns: Subjective criteria ('correctly implemented', 'properly handled')
Criteria that require human judgment to evaluate ('agent feels confident')
Missing a gad CLI verification command — every criterion must be checkable in under 60s

recommended_format_examples: - Passing handoff ID into child prompt and trusting it to call `gad handoffs complete`
- Opening TASK-REGISTRY.xml to check task status instead of `gad tasks list`
anti_patterns: Generic negations ('don't do bad things') without a specific behavior named
Anti-patterns that don't correspond to observed failure modes in ERRORS-AND-ATTEMPTS.xml

recommended_format_examples:
1. Before dispatching: confirm the worker loop — not the child — owns completeHandoff.
2. After child exits: worker calls gad handoffs complete immediately.
3. DO NOT pass handoff ID into child prompt.
4. If child exits non-zero: worker calls gad handoffs unclaim.
5. Verify: gad handoffs show <id> must show completed_at non-null.
anti_patterns: Steps that are out of causal order (verify before dispatch, review after action)
Negative constraints listed only in anti_patterns, not inline where the agent executes them
Missing a verification step — every workflow must end with an observable check
More than 8 steps — restructure into sub-workflows or collapse compound steps

recommended_format_examples:
- **Symptom**: completed_at null on closed handoffs. Cause: child was given responsibility it cannot fulfill.
- **Recovery**: worker calls complete retroactively; sweep with gad handoffs sweep.
anti_patterns: Failure modes that are just anti-patterns restated without symptom/recovery structure
Missing a recovery path — every failure mode must name what to do when it occurs
Linking to files the agent cannot read (private paths, generated outputs)
More than 5 references — list only load-bearing context, not tangential reading
